item.title: Why Rust CLI Tools Feel Great: ripgrep Searches 100GB in ~10MB — and It Isn't a 'Rust Magic'
item.description: The 'ripgrep searches 100GB in 10MB' claim has no official source — I checked BurntSushi's blog, the biggest single-file benchmark is 13GB of subtitles. But the underlying principle is real, and I proved it: on a 2-core box, 256MB/1GB/4GB corpora, ripgrep's RSS barely moves (7MB flat) while a 'read everything into memory' implementation balloons to 4GB. The secret is bounded memory + streaming fixed buffers, not Rust speed. Full reproducible code open-sourced.

item.title: Mercury 2.5: 1107 tok/s Is Inception's Number, 770 Is the Independent One
item.description: Inception's diffusion LLM Mercury 2.5 hit HN: officially 1107 tok/s, 260K context, launch discount at $0.04/$0.15. Artificial Analysis independently measured 770.4 tok/s (2nd of 184 models) and a 12-point intelligence score (median). Both numbers are true — the measurement gap is the point.
